doc.title: Ray Drummond interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003

title: How he composes: sketchbooks, piano and Finale
summary: He describes completing sketches, writing at the piano, and wanting to learn Finale, mentioning Kenny Werner's computer composing.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Have you ever had an instance where you wrote something and you were thinking this came from somewhere, but it was a while before you placed where that, maybe a little piece of musical inspiration came from?

Oh I’m sure. I mean I can’t think of anything right off the bat. I mean as a composer, the whole process of composing is such an incredibly complex, I mean it can become very simplified on one level but the process itself is a pretty complex sort of system because I mean I’ve composed songs — I mean I have sketch books filled of ideas. And from time to time I’ll pull out an idea and say oh — and complete it. Because it’s obvious that I was pointing at something, now I hear the whole thing. I just play it and say oh shit! That’s the composition.
Do you write at the piano?

Yeah I write at the piano, can write at the bass, sometimes write without anything around. That doesn’t happen very often but it has happened a couple of times where all of a sudden something comes to me and I just write it out. But the piano has probably been the resource that I’ve used the most for composing. One of these days I’m going to get Finale totally under my fingers. That’ll become a composing tool for me. Finale, Sibelius or one of those programs. Because they’ve become highly evolved now and they can be used as a composer’s tool rather than just — I know for instance Kenny Werner uses the computer a great deal in composing. For a time Billy Hart and I used to play together in Kenny’s trio and during that time he had just discovered how he could compose with a Mac powerbook and Finale, and a keyboard, you know a small synthesizer keyboard, and so he was taking that on the road, you know, writing all sorts of stuff out. Because he can print it right there and try to play it later.
